2. The facts leading to this Rule, in short, are that the petitioner Chittagong Textile Mills Ltd. hereinafter referred to as the Company is a limited liability company incorporated and registered under the Companies Act, 1913 and the said Company has its office and factory premises at North Kattali, PS Pahartali, Chittagong, and the Senior Manager is the Chief Executive thereof. The respondent No. 1 is the Chairman, Labour Court at Chittagong and respondent No. 2 was a worker under the petitioner in the Drawing Department of Mill No. 2, Shift-B till his dismissal from service by order dated 22.2.83 of the petitioner. The respondent No. 2 filed Complaint Case No. 116 of 1983 in the Court of respondent No. 1 (Chairman, Labour Court, Chittagong) under section 25 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965, hereinafter referred to as "the said Act" stating inter alia that he was a permanent worker under the petitioner and he had a clean service record and discharged his duty according to instructions of his superiors. He was served with a charge-sheet dated 5.1.83 for misconduct and he submitted explanation dated 6.1.83 denying the allegations brought against him. 

 4. The petitioner appeared in the Labour Court and contested the case by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the complaint petition and stating inter alia that two reports were received on 1.1.83 addressed to the Assistant Manager (Spinning) to the effect that on 1.1.83 one Mr. Manindra Dey found smell of burning of cotton in Mill No. 2 and when he examined the combing machine he found from line that Drawing machine No. 4 was out of order and when he enquired into the matter from the respondent No. 2 the latter suppressed the fact and stated that such smell was coming from outside. But on checking it was found that the machine was jammed and one of the brackets of the machine was broken. In another report it was mentioned that due to serious neglect of duty of the respondent No. 2 machine No. 4 caught fire and two bracket roller carrier wheels and one bracket were broken into pieces. On the above reports the respondent No. 2 was charged for his serious neglect of duty.
